thread:
alex.k: Heads-up — during a DR drill we tried failing over traffic to eu-west-1 and saw a bunch of app errors: KMS decrypts are failing for some DEKs. Errors vary between AccessDeniedException and InvalidCiphertextException. Anyone seen this when using multi-region keys (MRKs) across accounts?

maria.s: Yup, seen similar. Quick checklist: was the ciphertext generated by a primary in a different account/region? MRK replicas can decrypt but you still need policy/grants in the replica account.

sahil: To add — CloudTrail will tell you which key ARN the request hit. Look for kms:Decrypt events and the "keyId" field. If it hits a replica ARN but caller isn't authorized on that replica -> AccessDenied. If the ciphertext is from a non-MRK key and you try to use a different key -> InvalidCiphertext.

ajex: @maria.s typo — meant to say alex.k :p

maria.s: heh. Also check the encryption context. If the ciphertext was created with an encryption context and the decrypt call doesn't supply the exact same context, KMS returns InvalidCiphertext (or denies).

jordan: Example CLI repro we used in the drill:
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://dek.enc --region eu-west-1 --key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:222222222222:key/abcd-1111 
```
Result: AccessDenied if key policy/grant missing on the replica account.

alex.k: Our pattern: service A (acct 111) encrypts DEKs with primary in us-east-1, then we try to decrypt in eu-west-1 using a replica in acct 222. Sounds like some DEKs decrypt fine and some fail — could that be because some DEKs were produced earlier (pre-replication) vs later?

maria.s: Yeah. If ciphertext was produced by a key that wasn't yet replicated (or produced by a non-MRK key), replicas won't be able to decrypt. Also if the ciphertext embeds a key-id referencing the originating key ARN rather than the MRK id, KMS may treat it as non-replicable.

sahil: Another gotcha: grants. If the primary account issued grants to a role in acct 111, those grants don't automatically exist on the replica. Either replicate grants via cross-account replication (if allowed) or ensure the replica key policy allows the principal in acct 111 to call Decrypt on the replica.

amy.p: From a compliance/audit POV, we need to record which account/region actually performed the decrypt. CloudTrail shows the decrypt event region and keyId; ensure we log that with the request id in our DR report.

jordan: Practical runbook steps I recommend:
1) Check CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt events around the timestamp, note keyId and sourceIPAddress.
2) If AccessDenied: inspect replica key policy and grants (describe-key, list-grants).
3) If InvalidCiphertext: confirm ciphertext was generated by an MRK or a matching replica. Re-encrypt with local replica if needed.
4) Check encryption context exact match.
5) If many objects: consider a controlled rewrap job that re-encrypts DEKs under the local replica key (use an agent with principal permitted to Decrypt in origin and Encrypt in target).

alex.k: For rewrap, do we need plaintext material on disk? Our preference is re-encrypt server-side (Decrypt then Encrypt in memory). Any secure patterns to avoid long-lived plaintext?

sahil: Keep plaintext in-memory only; stream rewraps. Use ephemeral worker instances with no disks, EBS encryption, and shred memory on exit. Also rotate worker role credentials frequently. Ideally, do rewrap via a job that uses KMS ReEncrypt API (ReEncrypt allows re-encrypting ciphertext under a new key without exposing DEK plaintext to you).

maria.s: Note: ReEncrypt still needs Decrypt permission on origin and Encrypt on destination. If origin is in a different account, ensure those permissions are present. If cross-account policies are complex, consider temporary cross-account role assumption with least privilege.

kms-bot: INFO: Observability tip — KMS Decrypt events include "grantTokens" in the CloudTrail event if a grant token was used. Missing grant tokens when a grant exists can cause an API call to fail during rapid grant issuance.

alex.k: Good to know. Any recommendation around alias/key naming to make failover simpler?

amy.p: We standardize alias names across regions and accounts (alias/appname/mrk) so code can reference alias instead of explicit ARNs. But aliases are region+account-scoped; your deployment mapping must resolve the right alias per region/account. Document that mapping in runbook.

jordan: I'll open an ops ticket to update the DR runbook with the rewrap procedure, CloudTrail queries, and permission checklist. @sahil can you draft the minimal IAM/key policy snippet for cross-account replica decrypt?

sahil: Yep, will draft. High-level snippet: allow kms:Decrypt for the specific role ARN in the other account with Condition on kms:ViaService or aws:SourceAccount where appropriate. Will post in the ticket.

alex.k: Thanks folks — saved us from surprises during the next drill. If anyone has a short script for automated CloudTrail search + list of failing ciphertexts, drop it here.

maria.s: I'll paste a small Athena query later for searching Decrypt failures by errorCode.

amy.p: tagging compliance to review when ticket is ready. :white_check_mark:
